newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says A$ volatility delayed Dec rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says A$ volatility delayed Dec rate cut.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Tuesday that volatility in the foreign exchange market delayed the announcement of the 0.5 percentage point interest rate cut which was eventually announced on December 11.
The bank also said that financial markets had responded well to the three interest rate cuts announced in 1996.
The bank said that in timing interest rate changes, it took into account a wide range of factors including the state of the financial markets.

"Given the volatility of the foreign exchange market at the time of the December board meeting (on December 3), which included a fall in the exchange rate of about US three cents overnight, the bank felt it would have been inappropriate to reduce interest rates, and deferred the change until later in the month when market conditions had settled somewhat," it said. The cut took the official overnight cash rate to 6.0 percent.
The bank noted that around half of the 21 policy changes announced since 1990 had not occurred on the morning after the RBA board had met for its monthly meeting.
"Notwithstanding the volatility in the exchange rate in early December, financial markets overall responded well to the easings of monetary policy over the second half of 1996," the RBA said.
The bank said the reduction in overnight rates had been fully reflected in yields along the entire yield curve out to 10 years.
"That is, the curve moved down in parallel over the half year, an indication that capital markets viewed the easings as fully justified by the inflationary outlook," the RBA said.
The RBA also said the exchange rate had shown little net change in trade weighted terms over the second half of the year, although it fell somewhat against a stronger U.S. dollar.
